interpretation_note: Mechanical: points differential is a near-tautological predictor of wins, so a high value here validates the transcription, not the model. It is published as a data check.

Tests whether scoring offence and scoring defence move together across clubs. A value near zero supports treating the two legs of a same-game parlay as separable; a large value would mean independent-parlay maths is wrong for that pairing.
Same-game, same-model leg correlation. This is the number that decides whether a side+total same-game parlay may be priced as independent. n is the count of games with both legs graded.
Blowouts and shootouts are separate phenomena in this sample if this is near zero. Used to decide whether a 'parlay the favourite and the over' story has any basis.

Calibration of the originated total. A correlation near zero with a mean error near zero would mean the model is well-centred but uninformative; the signed mean error is reported on the validation page.

Requires a verified opening and closing price. No official NFL price source exists (nfl.com/odds/ is the NFL 404 page), so this cannot be computed without a third-party book, which the official-source-only rule forbids.
Requires official player prop prices and official per-player stat lines. NFL.com publishes injury designations and depth charts (both captured) but no prop prices.

Computable in principle: depth deficiency is captured for NE and DET, and both clubs' Week 10 games are in the slate. It is not computable yet because the Week 10 games have not been played, so n = 1 at most. Deferred to the Week 11 refresh.
